title: Using the Purpose Anchored Team (PAT™) Framework to Diagnose Team Performance Problems: An Executive-Team Coaching Case
abstract: Team performance problems may appear as conflict, slow decisions, repeated escalation or weak accountability, yet these symptoms may be generated by conditions at systemic levels. This paper introduces the Purpose Anchored Team (PAT™) Framework as a theory-informed diagnostic architecture for team performance. PAT™ does not propose another list of team-effectiveness factors. Instead, it uses stakeholder-derived team purpose as an organising criterion for locating performance problems within the team, within the organisation or in changing ecosystem demands. A 10-month executive-team coaching case illustrates the diagnostic sequence from presenting symptoms to problem formulation informed by multiple case data sources and established theory, intervention locus and operating changes. Data included interviews, coaching observations, organisational documents, decision records, pulse measures, stakeholder feedback and practitioner notes. PAT™ subsequently informed interventions in purpose clarification, decision architecture, organisational reinforcement and active learning routines. Descriptive changes are reported without claiming causal effectiveness or empirical validation of the framework.

journal.name: International Journal of Evidence Based Coaching & Mentoring
